question: What was the primary framework used to interpret mental illness in traditional Nigerian societies?
explanation: Traditional Nigerian communities historically viewed mental illness through spiritual and supernatural lenses rather than biomedical ones. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h1)

question: Why is understanding traditional beliefs in mental health still relevant for contemporary psychiatric nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: Traditional herbal remedies have completely replaced psychotropic drugs
options.B: The government requires nurses to be certified traditional birth attendants
options.C: Biomedical interventions are strictly forbidden in rural healthcare centers
options.D: Many patients consult traditional healers before seeking formal medical care

explanation: Because traditional and spiritual options remain a first-line resort for many families, nurses must navigate these cultural realities respectfully. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h1)

question: Which facility is recognized as a pioneering institution in the history of formal Nigerian psychiatric care?
explanation: Aro Asylum, established in 1947, was a major milestone in the transition toward institutional psychiatric care in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h2)

question: What was the primary operational focus of early psychiatric asylums during the colonial period?
explanation: Early asylums prioritized keeping patients contained and managing institutional order rather than providing active therapeutic rehabilitation. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h2)

question: Who developed the pioneering Aro Village System in the 1950s?
explanation: Professor Lambo pioneered the Aro Village System to integrate psychiatric treatment with local community living structures. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h3)

question: What is the primary advantage of the village-based psychiatric care model over traditional institutional asylums?

options.A: It preserves social connections and prevents institutional neurosis
options.B: It eliminates the need for any psychotropic medications
options.C: It ensures complete financial independence for every patient
options.D: It relies exclusively on high-tech diagnostic machinery

explanation: By housing patients within normal communities rather than isolated wards, the model maintains social ties and avoids the stagnation of long-term institutionalization. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h3)

question: Which outdated colonial legislation governed Nigerian mental health care for over six decades before its repeal?
explanation: The Lunacy Act of 1958 treated mental illness through a punitive, criminalized framework until it was replaced by modern legislation. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h4)

question: What major structural change was introduced by the passage of the National Mental Health Act 2021?

options.A: It abolished psychiatric nursing as a specialized training program
options.B: It mandated that all traditional healers must close their spiritual centers permanently
options.C: It replaced the old Lunacy Act and introduced explicit human rights protections for patients
options.D: It transferred all psychiatric funding entirely to private international donors

explanation: The 2021 Act modernized legal protections, moving away from criminalization toward safeguarding the fundamental human rights of individuals with mental disorders. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h4)

question: How has the primary role of the psychiatric nurse shifted in modern Nigerian healthcare settings?

options.A: From basic custodial containment to holistic psychosocial rehabilitation
options.B: From active clinical care to strictly administrative record keeping
options.C: From independent bedside practice to unsupervised medical prescribing
options.D: From community outreach work to exclusive laboratory diagnostics

explanation: Modern psychiatric nursing emphasizes therapeutic communication, rehabilitation, and active patient engagement rather than just watching over closed wards. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h5)

question: A psychiatric nurse in a primary health clinic is asked to train general community health workers on identifying common mental disorders. Which modern concept does this action reflect?

options.B: Complete reliance on traditional spiritual healing
options.C: Integration of mental health into primary health care
options.D: Exclusive use of high-security asylum management

explanation: Training primary health workers decentralizes care and makes mental health services accessible at the grassroots level. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h5)

question: What is a major workforce challenge currently facing the Nigerian mental health sector?

options.A: A complete lack of accredited nursing schools nationwide
options.B: Severe brain drain and emigration of trained personnel
options.C: Mandatory retirement ages set at thirty years old
options.D: An overwhelming surplus of licensed psychiatric nurses

explanation: The emigration of skilled healthcare professionals has left psychiatric facilities across Nigeria chronically understaffed. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h6)

question: Why does societal stigma continue to negatively impact mental health outcomes in Nigeria?

options.A: It drives individuals toward secretive or harmful alternative options instead of care
options.B: It eliminates the need for any psychotropic medications in public hospitals
options.C: It forces the government to build more community health centers
options.D: It automatically guarantees free medical care for all diagnosed patients

explanation: Fear of judgment and discrimination often leads families to delay seeking professional medical help, worsening long-term outcomes. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h6)
